segments.label: Shiplog
segments.text: This is Shiplog: a personal dev board that keeps itself in sync with GitHub. It follows one loop. Plan, code, log, and share.

segments.label: Connect
segments.text: Sign in with GitHub, then choose which repos Shiplog can read through a GitHub App. Every repo becomes a project, and your real contribution year sits on top. Click any day to see what you worked on.

segments.label: 1 · Plan
segments.text: Plan. Each project gets its own kanban board. Open GitHub issues sync in as cards, right next to your private to-dos.

segments.label: 2 · Code
segments.text: Code. Signed GitHub webhooks move the cards for you. Open a pull request that says fixes number twelve, and card twelve moves to in progress. Mark it ready, it's in review. Merge it, and it's done.

segments.label: In 3D
segments.text: Prefer 3D? The galaxy view turns every column into a planet, with its cards orbiting as little ships you can fly between them.

segments.label: 3 · Log
segments.text: Log. Every evening, Gemini turns the day's commits, issues and pull requests into a short journal entry you can edit. Each week becomes a summary with CV-ready bullet points. Private repos never leave the app.

segments.label: 4 · Share
segments.text: Share. Switch on a public page, and anyone can upvote your roadmap and read a changelog that your merged pull requests write for you.

segments.label: shiplog-silk.vercel.app
segments.text: Plan, code, log, share. That's Shiplog, built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and Postgres, and deployed on Vercel.
